### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/embedder-openai`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **11** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/shared.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/shared.json`, `packages/spec/src/shared/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via OpenAIEmbedder (symbol, a top-level class), estimateTokens (symbol, a top-level function), maxInputTokens (symbol, a field of class OpenAIEmbedder; a field of interface OpenAIEmbedderOptions))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/shared.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/shared.json`, `packages/spec/src/shared/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **69** of **252** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3ee24976fa845efd917d603017e67b43b8c022b1` — the merge of head `f4777fc327755a52e73ec78f62c425fa4f17881c` into base `bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3ee24976fa845efd917d603017e67b43b8c022b1 && git checkout 3ee24976fa845efd917d603017e67b43b8c022b1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09 f4777fc327755a52e73ec78f62c425fa4f17881c && git checkout -B drift-repro bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09 && git merge --no-ff f4777fc327755a52e73ec78f62c425fa4f17881c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bc3ec37a669f1b80c393e31393caea49fb4f7b09` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `183346bd87274ce26d8d91f585562e73169c43a2`
Local-runs: none
Scope: `packages/spec/src/shared/token-estimate.ts`, `packages/spec/src/shared/index.ts` + `packages/spec/src/shared/token-estimate.test.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/shared.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/shared.json`, `packages/plugins/embedder-openai/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/embedder-openai/src/__tests__/openai-embedder.test.ts`, `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`, `.changeset/37093-embedder-input-limit.md` + read, not reviewed: `AGENTS.md` (Prime Directive 2, Post-Task Checklist step 3), `.changeset/config.json`, `packages/spec/src/contracts/embedder.ts`, `packages/plugins/embedder-openai/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/package.json`, `packages/services/service-knowledge/src/knowledge-service.ts`, `packages/plugins/knowledge-memory/src/index.ts`

First review of this PR. Inputs read: card #37093 (body and its seven comments, among them rulings 7149124439, 7150730452 and 7151457223 and the dev report 7151644265), the PR body at this head, the full diff from the merge base `355c73c7` (9 files), the files at this head, and the 74 check-runs on this head (62 success, 12 skipped, none failed). The zone's conclusions were not taken as input; each claim below was read in the code.

### ① Derived judgments

Published surface, read at this head:

- `@objectstack/spec/shared` gains three names, all from `src/shared/token-estimate.ts`: `estimateTokens (function)`, `TOKEN_ESTIMATE_MARGIN (const)`, `ASCII_RUN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN (const)`. `api-surface/shared.json` and `export-origins/shared.json` each gain exactly those three lines, in sort order, with the right origin and kind. No other baseline is owed: the module holds no schema, so the authorable surface does not move.
- `estimateTokens(text: string): number`: named and typed right. Pure, no import, no state.
- `ASCII_RUN_CHARS_PER_TOKEN` is `Object.freeze({ letters: 4, digits: 3, mixed: 2 } as const)`. It is frozen at run time and read-only in the type, so a consumer cannot mutate it and the estimate reads it safely. See N2 for the literal types.
- `TOKEN_ESTIMATE_MARGIN = 1.1`: a plain `const`.
- `IEmbedder` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/embedder.ts`) is not in the diff.
- `embedder-openai`: `KNOWN_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS` is a module-private table, not an export. The one new public member is `OpenAIEmbedderOptions.maxInputTokens?: number`, an optional field, so every existing options literal still compiles.

The formula against ruling C (7150730452), term by term in the code:

- An ASCII run is `[A-Za-z0-9]+`. Letters only counts ceil(n / 4), digits only ceil(n / 3), letters and digits together ceil(n / 2). Any other character ends the run. This is ruling C exactly.
- A CJK character or full-width mark counts 1.5: the ranges are CJK Symbols and Punctuation, kana, Extension A, the Unified block, Hangul syllables, the compatibility block, Halfwidth and Fullwidth Forms, and Extensions B to G.
- Any other non-whitespace character counts 1; whitespace counts 0.
- The sum is multiplied by 1.1 and rounded up. The `1e-9` subtraction is sound: every sum is a multiple of 0.5, so every true product is a multiple of 0.55 and none sits within `1e-9` above an integer; the term only removes binary noise (10 × 1.1).
- Empty string: 0. ASCII whitespace only: 0. A CJK character between two ASCII runs ends the first and starts the second. Digits with separators (`12,800,000`): each group is its own digit run and each comma counts 1.
- One departure, in the safe direction: S1.

The refusal in `embed()`:

- The measuring loop runs over all inputs before the batch loop, so nothing is fetched when any input is over. The comparison is `estimate > limit`, so an input exactly at the limit is sent.
- The message names the 0-based index, the estimate, the limit and the model, says "Split the text below the limit", and ends "Nothing was sent."
- With no limit (unknown model, no option) the loop is skipped whole.

Option validation: `maxInputTokens` is refused at construction unless `Number.isInteger(v) && v >= 1`. So 0, a negative number, 1.5, `NaN`, `Infinity` and a string all throw "maxInputTokens must be a positive integer, got …". An explicit value wins over the table in both directions.

The unknown-model warning: one `console.warn` per instance, built from a list, so a model missing both options gets one message naming both. It is documented in three places: the option's TSDoc, the changeset (including the case of an app that set only `maxBatchSize` and now warns again) and `knowledge-rag.mdx`.

Provider limits in `KNOWN_MAX_INPUT_TOKENS`:

- Every row agrees with the source the code comment cites, as this reviewer knows those pages: OpenAI 8192 for all three models; DashScope `text-embedding-v3` 8192, `-v2` and `-v1` 2048; BigModel `embedding-3` 3072 and `embedding-2` 512; SiliconFlow `BAAI/bge-m3` 8192 and `BAAI/bge-large-zh-v1.5` / `-en-v1.5` 512.
- Not verified here: none of the four provider pages was re-read at the source in this review (read-only shape, no web read). The DashScope, BigModel and SiliconFlow rows in particular rest on the dev's reading of 2026-11-24.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes`: right, and present line-initial in the changeset and the PR body. The spec change is a widening only: three exports added, nothing removed or retyped. No arm is written, which the rule allows ("at most one arm").
- `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. No schema, key, accepted value or metadata type moves; the authorable-surface shards are untouched.
- Levels: the changeset says `@objectstack/spec` patch and `@objectstack/embedder-openai` patch. That is the level AGENTS.md sets: "`none` takes `patch`; a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`". New exports alone do not take minor under this repo's rule. Both packages sit in the one `fixed` group, so they release together.
- The embedder's behaviour does tighten at run time: a call that used to return now throws. It is not a change to a published accept set of the spec, and the changeset states it under "What to do". See S2 for the case that notice leaves out.

### ③ Boundary flags

- File surface: all nine paths are inside the claim (7147460438): `embedder-openai`, one shared module in spec plus the two baselines it regenerates, the docs page, the changeset.
- Placement in `spec/shared`, measured against Prime Directive 2 ("No business logic in `packages/spec`"): accepted. The card names the place; `embedder-openai` depends on `@objectstack/spec` alone and `service-knowledge` on `core`, `service-settings` and `spec`, so spec is the only common package; `resilientFetch` and `currencyForLocale` already ship from the same entry. A pure text measure carries no business rule.
- Dev report 7151644265: `open_questions` is empty. Its deviations are each answered: the merged warning (documented, see ①); the unpinned UUID and sha256 cases (ruled in 7151457223); the letters-class ablation being a no-op (the formula cases pin `letters: 4` by exact value); the full spec suite not re-run locally (the check-runs on this head ran it, all green).
- The PR body's Acceptance notes still end "so they are with the maintainer", written before ruling 7151457223 answered it. N5.
- SQL push-down: no query, no id materialisation and no join in this diff.
- Author: `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
- K at this head is 23. Size: 484 additions, 6 deletions, 9 files.
- No security finding.

### ④ Design judgment

`token-estimate.ts` against rulings A, C and 7151457223, and its first consumer:

M1 (must-fix) — the function's docblock states the opposite of the ruled residual. It says the estimate "is built to sit at or above OpenAI `cl100k` counts on Chinese, mixed Chinese/English and English-heavy text (long words, numbers, URLs, code, hashes and other identifiers)". Ruling 7151457223 records that a UUID estimates 28 against 40 and sha256 hex plus base64 71 against 81, and lets formula C stand on the condition that "the residual stays documented in the docblock and in `knowledge-rag.mdx`". The docs page does carry it. The docblock does not: no sentence in `token-estimate.ts` says a hash-, UUID- or base64-dense text can estimate below its real count, and the sentence above claims hashes are covered. This text ships in the published `.d.ts` of `@objectstack/spec/shared`, and it is what an app author sizing chunks reads. Closing it: take "hashes" out of the covered list and add the residual in the words the docs page already uses.

S1 (should-fix) — U+3000 (the ideographic space) counts 1.5, and three texts say whitespace counts 0. `isCjkOrFullWidth` is tested before the whitespace test and its first range starts at `0x3000`, so `estimateTokens('　')` is 2, not 0. The docblock says "An empty or all-whitespace text estimates 0" and "0 for whitespace", and the docs table and the changeset say the same. Chinese documents use this character for paragraph indents; the `zh-regulation-5` fixture holds one. The direction is safe (it over-counts), so this is a contract statement to correct, not a wrong refusal to fix. Closing it: either test whitespace first, or say in the docblock and the docs table that the full-width space counts as a full-width mark; and pin whichever is chosen.

`embedder-openai/src/index.ts` against the card: holds. Refusal before any request, whole call, message complete (①). No code in `packages/` calls `IEmbedder.embed` at this head, so the refusal reaches only an app's own adapter, which controls the texts it sends; "split the text" is an instruction such a caller can follow.

S2 (should-fix) — the changeset's notice leaves out the inputs that were embedded whole and are now refused. It says "A call that used to send a text over the model's limit — which the provider truncated — now fails instead". The estimate is conservative by design, so an input whose real count is under the limit can also fail: on Chinese text the estimate runs about 1.4 times the `cl100k` count in the fixtures, and on a 512-token BGE model, which tokenizes Chinese at about one token per character, a text of 311 to about 510 characters is now refused although it was never truncated. The ruling accepts this cost and the docs page states it. The changeset is the upgrade notice that ships in `CHANGELOG.md`, and it does not. Closing it: one sentence there, with the remedy (split lower, or set `maxInputTokens`).

Nits:

N1 (nit) — two comments describe a reader that does not exist yet. `shared/index.ts` says the estimate is "read by the embedders … and by knowledge chunking", and the docblock says a knowledge service "that sizes its chunks" uses it. Nothing in `service-knowledge` or `knowledge-memory` reads it at this head; that reader is #37098.

N2 (nit) — both constants publish literal types (`1.1`; `4`, `3`, `2`). The values changed twice in one day of rulings. A later change of value is then a change of published type that the name-level baselines do not show. Annotating them `number` would keep the type stable. The card asked for one function; the two constants are extra surface, named in the PR body and harmless.

N3 (nit) — the warning says the model "is not in the known-model table" whenever either option is missing. `embedding-2` is in the input-limit table and not in the batch table, so it is told it is in no table while its 512 limit is applied.

N4 (nit) — `Infinity` is refused, so a caller whose model really has no limit cannot say so; silencing the warning takes an invented large integer.

N5 (nit) — the PR body's last residual sentence ("The ruling lists both cases as pins … so they are with the maintainer") is out of date since 7151457223. Prose only.

N6 (nit) — only four table rows are pinned by a test (`bge-large-zh-v1.5` 512, `text-embedding-v2` 2048, and `embedding-3` and the OpenAI default as "above 2145"). A wrong digit in any other row turns nothing red.

N7 (nit) — emoji and rare ideographs (Extension B and later) count 1 and 1.5, and `cl100k` spends two to four tokens on each. The documented claim covers only the sampled classes, so nothing stated is false; a text dense in either is one more unsampled class beside hex and base64.

Tests that pin the new behaviour, read for ablation:

- Refusal removed: the first, third and fourth input-limit cases turn red. Refusal moved after the first request: `fetch` not called turns red.
- `>` changed to `>=`: the at-limit case (estimate 512, limit 512, sent unchanged) turns red.
- Message: index, model, estimate, limit and "Split the text below the limit" are each asserted by substring.
- Option validation: 0, -1, 1.5 and `NaN` each assert the throw.
- Unknown model: two calls of 20000 CJK characters are sent, `warn` called once, naming the model and `maxInputTokens`. The older batching case now needs both options to stay silent, which pins the merge.
- Formula: exact values pin 1.5 per CJK character, full-width punctuation, the margin, the rounding, whitespace 0, and each run class (`internationalization` 6, `12345678` 4, `a1b2c3d4` 5, `abcd` 2, `abcde` 3). Any class set to another divisor turns a case red.
- `cl100k` fixtures: 20 samples assert the estimate is at or above the recorded count. `en-digits-20` holds only with digits at 3 and `en-url-hex-id` only with mixed at 2, by the dev's ablation; that reading was not repeated here.
- Not pinned: U+3000 (S1), and seven of the eleven table rows (N6).

## 席位核对 — REWORK · L1 · head `183346bd87274ce26d8d91f585562e73169c43a2` · 2026-11-25T03:18Z

### Shape

- The PR is open, a draft, and based on `main`.
- `Fixes #37093` is right: the diff delivers every card line under rulings A → C and the residual ruling.
- No closing keyword binds another card.
- The declarations are `Clause-②: yes` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The rule asks for a `Skills-docs:` line only
  for a kind other than `none` or a `(narrowing)` arm, so none is owed here.
- The diff touches no governed surface (0 of 9 paths) and changes 490 lines. Not Tier H, so 「要你做什么：无」 is
  right.

### Gates at head (REST check-runs)

- 74 runs: 62 `success`, 12 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 pending.
- All 12 skips are on the expected-skip roster.
- Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check are `success`.
- The required set is green, apart from Lint UI, which is an expected skip.
- Test Core at head ran `token-estimate.test.ts` (28 tests) and `openai-embedder.test.ts` (27 tests).

### Premises measured

- The dependency intersection is `@objectstack/spec` alone.
- `spec/shared` already re-exports runtime helpers (`resilient-fetch`, `region-currency`).
- There is no `packages/spec/src/contracts` diff.
- cl100k fixtures:
  - All 20 recorded counts reproduce exactly with js-tiktoken 1.0.21 `cl100k_base`, run outside the repo.
  - Every estimate is at or above its count; the tightest is `en-numbers`, 48 against 45.
- Ablations reproduce:
  - digits → 4: `en-digits-20` red, plus 2 formula cases;
  - mixed → 4: `en-url-hex-id` red, plus 1;
  - letters: a no-op;
  - one token per run: 11 red, including all 8 English pins.
- The residual reproduces on samples of my own:
  - four UUIDs estimate 93 against cl100k 107;
  - a base64 string estimates 43 against 54.
- Provider limits were not re-fetched. The code table matches the body's cited table and the changeset.

### Done-when

- Every card line maps to code and a test:
  - over-limit refused, naming index, model, estimate and limit, with nothing sent;
  - an at-limit input sent unchanged;
  - per-model limits;
  - the override and its validation;
  - an unknown model warns once and is not limited;
  - the shared module on `@objectstack/spec/shared`;
  - the sampled cl100k pins.
- The one gap is the docblock half of "documented on its docblock" for the residual (M1).

### Accepted deviations

- The seat opened the PR and wrote its body on the maintainer's 「开 PR 放行」 (7149124439 ①). The dev session's
  `pr_create` and body edit were refused.
- UUID and sha256+base64 are not pinned, per 「C 照现在合入」 (7151457223).
- The letters-class ablation is a no-op, because that class is unchanged from A.
- The full spec suite was last run locally at `2724c5e4`. CI Test Core ran both changed test files at the head.

### Out of scope

- #37098 (open) carries `IEmbedder.maxInputTokens?`, the service learning the limit, and splitting.
- #37100 (open) carries `IEmbedder.model?`.
- The body names both.

### Changeset, `knowledge-rag.mdx` and the docblock, read sentence by sentence

- The changeset is in user terms and has a "What to do" paragraph.
- Its model limits and formula match the code, and it states the warning-merge consequence.
- The mdx residual paragraph matches the measurement.

### Landing terms

- K from the brief's formula (merge-base `355c73c7` → `origin/main` `893eac8b`) is 23.
- `landing-k.mjs` K from PRBASE `753aae6ded` is 4, under the hold of 15. Its locale and shared-budget legs are
  clean.
- `git merge-tree` against `origin/main` is clean, and main has touched none of the PR's 9 paths.
- The PR touches the `merge=os-regen` paths `packages/spec/api-surface/shared.json` and
  `packages/spec/export-origins/shared.json`. So arming owes the os-regen merge first (`os-regen-merge.sh`,
  landing-operations §A), with generated-artifact drift re-measured in the same act.

### Open items

- M1 (must-fix) — the `estimateTokens` docblock in `packages/spec/src/shared/token-estimate.ts` states a
  guarantee the PR measures as false.
  - It reads "built to sit at or above OpenAI `cl100k` counts on … English-heavy text (long words, numbers, URLs,
    code, hashes and other identifiers)". The PR's own Acceptance notes, and my readings, show hash, UUID and base64
    text below cl100k.
  - This TSDoc ships in `dist/*.d.ts` of the published `@objectstack/spec`.
  - Ruling 7151457223 requires the residual to be documented "in the docblock".
  - Fix:
    - drop "hashes" from the guarantee;
    - add the residual sentence as the mdx states it: random hex or base64 tokenizes at about 1–1.4 characters per
      token and can estimate below its real count;
    - align the `src/shared/index.ts` comment ("upper estimate") the same way.
  - Dev patch round. Re-run `check:generated` after it.
- S1 (should-fix) — the PR body's Acceptance notes still say the two residual cases "are with the maintainer".
  - Cite ruling 7151457223 (「C 照现在合入」: not pinned, no follow-up card until there is pull).
  - Say the docblock states the residual once M1 lands.
  - The seat owns this body, so the fix is a seat edit.
- N1 — 维护者速读 「出错会怎样」 could add the ruled residual: text dense with hashes or UUIDs can still be
  under-estimated and truncated.
- N2 — The changeset, the mdx and the `embed()` JSDoc say `embed()` "measures every input" before sending. That
  holds only when a limit applies: an unknown model with no `maxInputTokens` is not measured.
- N3 — `knowledge-rag.mdx`: "A provider sent a longer text truncates it" should read "A provider that is sent a
  longer text truncates it".
- N4 — The `CL100K_ENGLISH_SAMPLES` doc comment says one token per run was "the rule this module first shipped
  with". It never shipped; it was the first draft on this branch.
- **Contract review at this head:** 7151747480 (CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER), FAIL. Its M1 is this L1's M1. Fix its S1 in the same round: U+3000 counts 1.5 while the docs say whitespace is 0; align the code or the docs, and pin it. Fix its S2 too: the changeset must say that inputs under the real limit but over the estimate now fail (e.g. about 311–510 Chinese characters on a 512-token model).
- **S1 (PR body) is the seat's to fix**, since the seat wrote the body. It is done in the same stroke as this comment: the Acceptance note now cites 7151457223, and 维护者速读 names the hash/UUID gap.
- **Next:** one dev patch round for M1, the contract review's S1 and S2, and N2–N4. Then the seat reads the delta and runs a delta contract review. The zone lands it, with `os-regen-merge.sh` at arming.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `8007e0bfca9990a1cf1d013d955991e9a07e287e`
